description: Shadow Mode results: pessimistic ShadowMatcher (realistic queue-position fills, taker slippage, Binance fee schedule) driven by live TOPOS topology decisions on real Binance BTCUSDT futures market data

runs.value_model_note: value model .so file was not present on this run (lost between sessions on the instance); engine correctly fell back to running without it, not a crash, but this run's decisions did not use the value_pred signal at all

consistent_finding_across_both_runs.maker_ratio: 0.0% in both independent sessions -- not a single limit order filled via queue exhaustion in either run
consistent_finding_across_both_runs.net_pnl: deeply negative in both runs, entirely driven by taker fees on a strategy that trades far more often than it should for its edge size
consistent_finding_across_both_runs.root_cause: LIQUIDITY_PROVISION logic places limit orders at exactly best bid/best ask with queue_position initialized to the FULL resting volume at that level (often 4-25 BTC observed in logs); at Binance BTCUSDT liquidity and trade sizes (fractions of a BTC per aggTrade), exhausting that queue takes far longer than the time between our own CANCEL_ALL triggers (which fire very frequently -- TOXIC_VORTEX/anomaly regime dominates the decision stream, consistent with the earlier Predictive Power Check finding that TOXIC_VORTEX was the most common labeled regime in a comparable session)
consistent_finding_across_both_runs.consequence: the strategy as currently implemented is a pure taker strategy in practice, despite being designed to alternate between maker and taker behavior by regime; it pays the 0.04% taker fee on every fill with no offsetting maker rebate income, on a directional signal (IMPULSE, from earlier validation) whose edge (~IC 0.42 at 10-tick horizon) is far too small and far too short-lived to cover round-trip taker fees plus the adverse selection of trading through an already-thin book

what_this_answers: the partner's original question -- 'does the signal survive contact with real execution economics' -- is now answered: NO, not with this execution logic. The infrastructure (WS dual-stream, lock-free AttractorBridge, spinlock-guarded OMS, pessimistic queue-position matcher) all functioned correctly and as designed. The trading logic layered on top of it (naive best-bid/best-ask posting, immediate CANCEL_ALL on every anomaly tick) is not economically viable against real Binance BTCUSDT liquidity and fee structure.
not_yet_investigated: whether posting further from best bid/ask (accepting worse queue position but avoiding constant cancel/repost churn) would improve maker fill rate
whether reducing CANCEL_ALL sensitivity (the anomaly threshold itself, separate from the refit cooldown already tuned) would reduce unnecessary order churn
whether the MARKET_TAKER logic's fixed tiny size (0.001 BTC) combined with the short-lived IMPULSE signal is fundamentally fee-negative regardless of tuning, given known IC decay past ~10-50 ticks

true unrealized mark-to-market PnL was not tracked during the session, only realized PnL from actual fills plus the final forced cancellation of any remaining open orders (which have no PnL impact since they never filled)

diagnostic_experiment_isolating_root_cau.hypothesis: is zero maker fill rate caused by CANCEL_ALL churn frequency (VORTEX regime firing too often to let orders wait), or by queue depth (resting volume too large relative to trade flow)?
diagnostic_experiment_isolating_root_cau.method: modified engine to suppress cancel_all specifically on VORTEX/anomaly decisions, letting maker limit orders ride through anomalies for the full 120s session (still force-canceled at shutdown, no PnL impact since unfilled)
diagnostic_experiment_isolating_root_cau.conclusion: hypothesis REJECTED for churn frequency: even with 358 potential premature cancellations suppressed (orders allowed to sit through anomaly regimes for the entire session), maker_ratio remained exactly 0.0%. This confirms the root cause is queue depth, not cancellation frequency -- the strategy joins the queue behind the full resting volume at best bid/ask (4-25 BTC observed), and realistic BTCUSDT aggTrade flow over these session lengths is insufficient to exhaust that queue regardless of how long the order is allowed to wait. Tuning CANCEL_ALL sensitivity or cooldown parameters will not fix maker fill rate; the order placement logic itself (posting at the very back of a deep queue) is the structural problem.
diagnostic_experiment_isolating_root_cau.implication_for_future_work: a maker strategy on this instrument/liquidity profile would need either much larger size relative to queue depth (capital-intensive and risky), joining thinner price levels further from best bid/ask (worse expected fill price if it does fill), or abandoning passive queue-joining in favor of a different maker mechanism entirely (e.g. quote inside the spread, accept adverse selection risk explicitly). This was not tested further; it is a separate, larger design question.

thin_level_quoting_experiment.change: LIQUIDITY_PROVISION now scans top-3 bid/ask levels and quotes at the level with minimum resting volume, instead of always quoting at best bid/ask
thin_level_quoting_experiment.finding: improvement is real but tiny: maker_ratio rose from 0.0% to 0.4% (first-ever maker fill observed, at queue_position=0.002 when placed vs typical 4-25 at best bid/ask). NET PnL remains deeply negative in the same range as prior runs (-4.5 to -9.4). Thin-level quoting alone is insufficient.
thin_level_quoting_experiment.new_finding_from_log_inspection: a third interacting variable was identified: order REPOST frequency. LIQUIDITY_PROVISION reposts a fresh pair of orders every tick where n_open_orders()==0, and VORTEX/CANCEL_ALL fires very frequently (TOXIC_VORTEX dominates the decision stream). The combined effect is that even thin-queue orders rarely survive long enough between repost cycles for enough trade volume to accumulate against them -- it is not purely queue depth OR purely cancel frequency, but their interaction with how often EQUILIBRIUM reposts a fresh order after the previous one clears (whether by cancel or fill).
thin_level_quoting_experiment.next_experiment: give newly placed maker orders a minimum lifetime (e.g. do not reposition/replace on ordinary EQUILIBRIUM ticks while an order is already resting, and do not let VORTEX cancel an order younger than N ticks unless anomaly severity is extreme) to let queue exhaustion actually have time to occur

market_taker_debounce_breakthrough.root_cause_found: MARKET_TAKER decision fired on EVERY tick where the topology regime was IMPULSE, with no check for existing position -- since IMPULSE regime persists across multiple consecutive ticks (regimes don't flip every tick), the engine was sending a new 0.001 BTC market order on EVERY such tick, repeatedly paying the 0.04% taker fee to add to an already-held position rather than taking one position per signal occurrence. This explains the 190-360 taker fills seen in prior runs -- most were redundant re-entries into the same directional bet, not independent trading decisions.
market_taker_debounce_breakthrough.fix: added a position check before sending a new MARKET_TAKER order: skip if already positioned in the same direction (net_quantity > 0.0005 for BUY, < -0.0005 for SELL)

result.improvement_vs_prior_run: NET PnL improved from -10.98 to -0.92, an approximately 12x reduction in loss; filled_orders dropped from 360 to 31 (91% reduction), confirming most prior taker fills were redundant re-entries rather than independent decisions

market_taker_debounce_breakthrough.still_negative_because: gross PnL (0.048) still does not cover total fees (0.972) -- the ratio improved dramatically but the strategy is not yet profitable. Position is never explicitly closed when the signal fades (net_quantity=0.001 remained open at session end), meaning exits are implicit/accidental rather than designed.
market_taker_debounce_breakthrough.next_step: add explicit exit logic (e.g. close position when regime shifts away from IMPULSE, or after a fixed holding period) rather than relying on opposite-direction signals to naturally net out the position

explicit_exit_and_lifetime_tuning.description: Added explicit position exit (close via opposite-side market order when regime leaves IMPULSE), with symmetric debounce on both entry (MIN_ORDER_LIFETIME_TICKS) and exit (MIN_POSITION_HOLD_TICKS) to prevent re-creating the churning problem on the exit side.
explicit_exit_and_lifetime_tuning.conclusion: lifetime=100 reproducibly outperforms lifetime=15 across two independent live sessions (NET PnL -1.5 to -1.8 vs -4.77), rejecting the hypothesis that shortening the hold period toward the ~10-tick signal horizon (from the earlier Predictive Power Check) would improve results. The reverse held: more frequent entry/exit cycling at short lifetime increased fee drag faster than it captured signal edge. This is a methodologically important finding: parameters should not be tuned toward the raw signal-decay horizon without accounting for the fixed cost (fee) per cycle -- optimal holding period is a function of both signal decay AND transaction cost, not signal decay alone.
explicit_exit_and_lifetime_tuning.caveat: each run is a single ~150s live session on a live, non-repeatable market; the two lifetime=100 runs used different market windows (not a controlled A/B on identical data), so the exact PnL figures (-1.51 vs -1.84) reflect both the parameter and market variation. The qualitative ranking (100 clearly better than 15) is considered more reliable than the precise PnL values.

overall_progress_summary.still_not_profitable: yes -- gross PnL (0.06-0.20) still does not exceed total fees (1.6-2.0) in either lifetime=100 run; the strategy has gone from catastrophically unprofitable to modestly unprofitable, not to profitable

strict_maker_paradigm_severity_threshold.description: Full paradigm shift per lead's direction: zero taker fee rule (place_market_order never called), IMPULSE reinterpreted as price-improvement queue-jump maker order, VORTEX severity thresholding (only cancel_all when best_dist/epsilon ratio > 5.0, not on any epsilon breach) to stop VORTEX from dominating the decision stream and starving maker orders of any lifetime.

severity_ratio_distribution_measured.rationale: sits near p75-p90 across both measured sessions, filtering the bulk of mild epsilon breaches (median ratio ~1.5) while still catching genuine tail events

iteration_history.bug: cancel_all called every tick in IMPULSE branch with no debounce, causing 513 cancels vs 1 fill
iteration_history.note: artifact of near-zero trading activity, not a real result

iteration_history.result: 361 cancels vs 1 fill -- debounce alone insufficient, VORTEX branch (uncooled per lead's explicit request) was the dominant cancel source

iteration_history.finding: vortex_cancel_calls=296 vs impulse_replace_calls=128 over 1363 ticks -- confirmed VORTEX firing on 21.7% of ticks was structurally incompatible with any maker order surviving long enough to fill

iteration_history.result: canceled orders dropped 296+ -> 59, but filled_orders remained 0 in that specific run
canceled orders 72, filled orders=2, NET PnL=+0.0468 (first positive result of the entire session), zero fees (true maker-only)

strict_maker_paradigm_severity_threshold.current_status: first positive NET PnL achieved, but on a tiny sample (2 fills) in a single run. Not yet confirmed as reproducible -- the same severity-threshold configuration produced 0 fills in one run and 2 profitable fills in the next, both within the natural session-to-session market variation already documented earlier in this project. This must be repeated at least once more before being treated as a validated result, not a lucky window.
